say.text: A 64-year-old man has small bowel obstruction. His history says no previous abdominal surgery.
What is the most likely cause?

choices.label: Adhesive bands, the usual adult cause
Obstructed hernia at a groin orifice

say.text: Yes. With no previous surgery, adhesions are unlikely, so a surgical cause must be found, and hernia comes first.
Examine every hernial orifice, groins and femoral canals included, before you name a cause.
Tempting: adhesions are the commonest cause of adult small bowel obstruction overall, so they come to mind first.
Try again, and re-read the history line you skimmed past.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck the history line: no previous surgery changes the answer.

say.text: Common slip: adhesions explain every adult obstruction. In a virgin abdomen they are unlikely, so hernia comes first.
Right answer: an obstructed hernia at a groin orifice, checked before any tumour.
A 60-year-old woman has a painful, irreducible groin lump and has been vomiting since morning.
Which groin hernia is most likely to strangulate?

choices.label: Indirect inguinal hernia, the commonest groin type
Femoral hernia through the femoral canal
Direct inguinal hernia, a very common groin type

say.text: Yes. Femoral hernia has a narrow, rigid neck, so its contents strangulate more readily than in the inguinal types.
Among groin hernias, femoral has the highest strangulation risk. That answers a different question from which is commonest.
Tempting: the inguinal hernias are the common ones, so they feel like the dangerous ones. Frequency is a separate question.
Try again. Ask which neck is narrowest and most rigid.

sure_note.text: You were sure. Commonness and danger are different questions; check the neck of each sac.

say.text: Common slip: you read 'most common' as 'most likely to strangulate'. Inguinal hernias are commoner, but the femoral neck is narrow and rigid, so it strangulates most often.
A man has a tender, irreducible groin swelling. He is passing flatus, has no vomiting or distension, and his lactate is rising.
What is the mechanism?

choices.label: Only part of the bowel wall is trapped
A complete closed loop is trapped in the sac
A Meckel's diverticulum lies inside the sac

say.text: Yes. Richter's hernia traps only part of the bowel wall's circumference, so it can strangulate without complete obstruction.
That is why vomiting and distension can be absent while the bowel is already dying.
Tempting: strangulation feels like a closed loop that blocks completely, with vomiting and distension. Check what is actually trapped in this sac.
Try again. Ask whether the whole circle of the wall is caught.

sure_note.text: You were sure that strangulation means complete blockage. This is the commonest error with Richter's.

say.text: Common slip: strangulation always means complete obstruction. Richter's traps only part of the wall, so the lumen can stay partly open.
The right picture is part of the wall trapped and strangulated, with no complete obstruction.
Tempting: a Meckel's diverticulum is a classic content you remember, so it feels like the answer. A content label names an eponym, not a mechanism.
Try again. Ask what mechanism the stem describes.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so check that you are matching the mechanism, not the contents.

say.text: Common slip: Richter's and Littre's are the same hernia. Littre's contains a Meckel's diverticulum, while Richter's traps only part of the wall.
The stem describes partial wall strangulation, so the answer is Richter's.
A 62-year-old man has colicky abdominal pain and a palpable mass. CT shows intussusception.
Which management is right?
Yes. In an adult, intussusception usually has a pathological lead point, often a tumour, so resection is the treatment.
Enema reduction belongs to the child without peritonitis.
Tempting: intussusception and enema reduction are a familiar pair from childhood, so the enema is the reflex.
Try again. Which feature of this patient changes the cause and the treatment?

sure_note.text: You were sure, so check the age before choosing the pathway.

say.text: Common slip: intussusception always means an enema cure. A child's is usually idiopathic and reduces with an enema.
An adult's usually has a lead point, often a tumour, and is treated by resection.
Why is an adult's intussusception managed differently from a child's?

choices.label: Adult bowel wall is too thick for enema pressure
Adults usually have a lead point, often a tumour
Adult intussusception is usually ileocolic and idiopathic, as in children

say.text: Yes. In adults the lead point is usually a tumour, so the bowel is resected rather than reduced.
Tempting: the adult bowel feels different, so a physical reason seems plausible. The real difference is the cause: a lead point, often a tumour.
The explanation is the lead point, not the wall.
Tempting: the child's pattern feels universal, so it gets copied to adults. A child's intussusception is usually idiopathic; an adult's usually has a lead point.
A 9-month-old is resuscitated and stable, with no peritonitis. Ultrasound confirms intussusception.
Best next step?
Yes. Without peritonitis, perforation, shock or failed reduction, a child is reduced by enema under imaging.
Surgery is for those criteria, not for the diagnosis alone.
Tempting: obstruction in a child feels like a surgical emergency, so theatre looks like the safest route.
Try again. Which finding in the stem would change the plan?

sure_note.text: You were sure. Ask which finding would send this child to theatre, not which feels safest.

say.text: Common slip: surgery is the safe default. The criteria are peritonitis, perforation, shock or failed enema. Without them, the child is reduced without surgery.
Which finding means this child needs theatre rather than an enema?

choices.label: Colicky pain and vomiting for 12 hours

say.text: Yes. Peritonitis suggests perforation or dead bowel, one of the criteria for surgery.
Tempting: once the diagnosis is made, it feels as if it needs fixing in theatre. A confirmed intussusception is the indication for enema reduction.
The criteria decide the operation, not the scan.
Tempting: a child in pain and vomiting looks sick enough for surgery. Colicky pain and vomiting are the usual presentation.
They do not by themselves mean theatre; the surgical criteria do.
In an adult, what is the most common cause of large bowel obstruction?
Yes. Colorectal carcinoma is the commonest cause of adult large bowel obstruction. Diverticular disease and volvulus follow.
Tempting: diverticular disease is a familiar large bowel problem, so 'common' stretches into 'most common'.
In adults, carcinoma comes first and diverticular disease after it.
Tempting: sigmoid volvulus is the commonest colonic volvulus, so it feels like the big cause. But it is not the commonest cause of adult large bowel obstruction.
Carcinoma is.
Which is the commonest site of colonic volvulus?
Yes. The caecum is the commonest site of perforation in closed-loop obstruction.
Perforation follows the widest loop, by Laplace's law.
Tempting: the caecum is the famous perforation site, so it gets carried over to volvulus. The sigmoid is the commonest volvulus site.
Tempting: sigmoid volvulus is the commonest volvulus, so the sigmoid gets assumed to perforate too. Perforation follows the widest loop, which is the caecum.
A stable elderly man has no peritonitis. A plain film shows sigmoid volvulus.
Best first treatment, and what must follow?

choices.label: Endoscopic detorsion, then elective sigmoid colectomy
Endoscopic detorsion, then discharge once well

say.text: Yes. The loop is viable and there is no peritonitis, so detorsion comes first, with a flatus tube.
Sigmoid volvulus recurs often, so elective sigmoid colectomy follows, usually in the same admission.
Tempting: once the loop untwists, the job feels finished and the patient looks well.
Try again. What happens to the sigmoid after detorsion?

sure_note.text: You were sure that detorsion ends care. The sigmoid comes back, so the story is not finished.

say.text: Common slip: detorsion is the end of care. Sigmoid volvulus recurs often after detorsion, so elective sigmoid colectomy follows, usually in the same admission.
Tempting: volvulus sounds like an emergency, so resection feels safest. Before you resect, ask whether the bowel is gangrenous or perforated.
Try again. What state is the bowel in?

sure_note.text: You were sure. Check the bowel's state before choosing resection.

say.text: Common slip: every volvulus needs resection. Hartmann's is for gangrene, perforation or failed detorsion. This loop is viable, so detorsion comes first.
A stable 70-year-old woman has an obstructing carcinoma of the caecum.
Which operation is right?

choices.label: Self-expanding metallic stent as definitive treatment

say.text: Yes. Obstructing right-sided colon cancer is treated by right or extended right hemicolectomy with primary anastomosis.
Name the side of the tumour first; the operation follows from it.
Tempting: one 'colon cancer' operation is easy to recall, so the side gets skipped. Which side is the caecum on?
Try again. Name the side before the operation.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so name the side first.

say.text: Common slip: one operation fits all colon cancers. Left hemicolectomy suits left-sided tumours; the caecum is on the right.
Right-sided obstruction is treated by right hemicolectomy with primary anastomosis.
Tempting: a stent relieves obstruction without surgery, so it feels like a definitive answer.
Try again. Which side is a stent used for?

sure_note.text: You were sure that a stent is the answer. Check the side and the purpose.

say.text: Common slip: a stent is definitive treatment for any obstructing cancer. A self-expanding stent relieves malignant left-sided obstruction, as a bridge to surgery or as palliation.
A right-sided caecal tumour needs right hemicolectomy.
Plain film: a massively dilated loop arising from the pelvis, shaped like a coffee bean.
What is the diagnosis?
Yes. A coffee bean, or bent inner tube, on plain film is sigmoid volvulus.
Caecal volvulus looks different: a kidney-shaped caecum displaced to the left upper quadrant.
Tempting: a twisted, dilated loop on film sounds like the caecum. Look at where this loop arises from.
Try again. Which loop arises from the pelvis?

sure_note.text: You were sure. The shape and origin on film decide the site.

say.text: Common slip: any volvulus on film looks alike. Caecal volvulus shows a kidney-shaped or comma-shaped caecum displaced to the left upper quadrant.
The coffee bean arises from the pelvis and is the sigmoid.
Tempting: a mass-like loop on imaging makes you think of intussusception, so the volvulus signs get lost.
Try again. Is the coffee bean a volvulus sign or an intussusception sign?

sure_note.text: You were sure. Each sign belongs to one disease on one film.

say.text: Common slip: volvulus and intussusception share one sign list. Intussusception shows a target or pseudokidney on ultrasound and a claw on enema.
The coffee bean is a sigmoid volvulus sign on plain film.
Match each sign to the test that shows it.
Which pairing is correct?

choices.label: Claw sign: contrast enema; target sign: ultrasound
Claw sign: ultrasound; target sign: contrast enema
Bird's beak on enema: intussusception; target on film

say.text: Yes. The claw sign is seen on contrast enema in intussusception. The target, or doughnut, sign is seen on ultrasound.
Each sign belongs to one disease and one test.
Tempting: both signs come from imaging of the same condition, so the test gets swapped. The claw is an enema sign; the target is an ultrasound sign.
Tempting: the bird's beak is a classic sign, so it gets carried over to intussusception. Bird's beak belongs to volvulus on contrast enema.
The target sign belongs to ultrasound of intussusception.
Close: in a virgin abdomen the list is hernia first, then tumour.
Examine every hernial orifice before you name a tumour.
At operation, a groin hernia sac contains a Meckel's diverticulum.
Which eponym?
Yes. Littre's hernia contains a Meckel's diverticulum.
Richter's is defined by part of the wall, not by contents.
Tempting: both are strangulated-hernia eponyms, so they blur. Richter's traps part of the wall; the Meckel's content makes it Littre's.
Tempting: any eponym with a loop in the sac seems to fit. Maydl's has a W-shaped loop; Meckel's in the sac is Littre's.
A hernia sac holds a healthy-looking loop, part of a W-shaped double loop.
Where is the strangulated loop in Maydl's hernia?

choices.label: Only part of the wall of the loop in the sac
Inside the abdomen, not in the sac
The loop in the sac, as in any strangulated hernia

say.text: Yes. Maydl's hernia contains a W-shaped loop, and the strangulated loop lies inside the abdomen.
Examine the intra-abdominal limb, not only the sac contents.
Tempting: partial-wall trapping is the other famous hernia idea. That is Richter's; Maydl's is a W-shaped loop.
Tempting: the sac holds the loop you can see, so it gets blamed. In Maydl's, the strangulated loop lies inside the abdomen.
Tempting: a familiar large bowel problem. Ask which cause is commonest, not which is best known.
Try again, or see why.
Tempting: a dramatic emergency is memorable. Ask which cause is commonest, not most dramatic.
Try again, or see why.
Tempting: the caecum is famous for perforation, but this question is about volvulus.
Try again, or see why.
Tempting: the volvulus site gets carried over. Perforation follows a different rule.
Try again, or see why.
Tempting: a confirmed diagnosis feels like an indication. Ask which finding changes the route.
Try again, or see why.
Tempting: a child in pain looks surgical. Ask which finding is more than the usual presentation.
Try again, or see why.
Tempting: both signs come from imaging, so they swap. Ask which test shows which.
Try again, or see why.
Tempting: a famous sign gets carried over. Ask which disease owns the bird's beak.
Try again, or see why.
Yes. The sigmoid is the commonest site of volvulus.
In closed-loop large bowel obstruction, which is the commonest site of perforation?
Tempting: the transverse colon sounds mobile, but ask which loop twists most often.
Try again, or see why.
Tempting: the transverse colon has a long mesentery, so it feels like the twisting loop. The sigmoid is the commonest site of volvulus.
Tempting: the rectum is where the block feels lowest. Ask which loop is widest.
Try again, or see why.
Tempting: the block is distal, so the rectum feels at risk. Perforation follows the widest loop, which is the caecum.
